--- title: "The Forester's Forecast" --- **The Forester's Forecast** is an interview series dedicated to the people behind forest biometrics and forest analytics — the scientists, researchers, and analysts whose work quietly shapes how we understand, measure, and manage forests. The show features three series: the flagship interview series, exploring the careers and life stories of professionals; **The Grad Student Spotlight**, which highlights graduate students, showcasing their research and career goals; and **A Band of Biometricians**, a roundtable series where multiple proffesionals are gathered discuss current hot topics in the field. Your host, **Micky G. Allen II, Ph.D., CF**, is a consulting forest biometrician and senior forest analyst at Larson & McGowin, LLC, working in forest inventory and harvest planning. Micky created The Forester's Forecast to document the careers and stories of the people who form the backbone of forest biometrics. ::: {.cell} ::: ## Latest Episodes ### The Forester's Forecast #### Episode 20: Dr. Robert Froese *September 29, 2026*
My guest this episode is Dr. Robert Froese, Professor and Endowed Chair in Forest Growth and Yield at the University of Alberta. He joined from a campground in the Canadian Rockies. We talk about his path from UBC to the University of Idaho, 18 years at Michigan Tech, and his return to Canada. He's now leading a $5.9M project to rethink how Alberta models forest growth and yield. ### Grad Student Spotlight #### Grad Student Spotlight - Episode 3: Olakunle Joshua *January 30, 2025*
Joshua is a PhD student in the SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry and founder of The Achiever's Gathering, Nigeria (TAGNG). ### A Band of Biometricians #### A Band of Biometricians #2: The U.S. National Scale Volume and Biomass estimation system *September 03, 2026*
On this episode of A Band of Biometricians (a series from The Forester's Forecast), Micky Allen sits down with four of the people behind the USDA Forest Service's National-Scale Volume and Biomass (NSVB) system — Aaron Weiskittel (University of Maine), John Coulston (formerly USFS Southern Research Station, now NCASI), Jim Westfall (USFS Northern Research Station, lead author), and Phil Radtke (Virginia Tech).
